title: Profile-driven p95/p99 attribution and tokens/sec regression dashboards per endpoint/model/region
creator: Sasha Kim
description: Add a profile-driven system for attributing p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec regressions to route + model + region slices, produce dashboards with percentile heatmaps, and wire automatic regression detection and alerting into Console. The goal is to make deviations from baseline visible by workload profile (short chat, long completion, embeddings-heavy) and enable on-call to quickly identify whether regressions are model, routing, or infra related.
background: Current latency dashboards provide rollups and some per-route views but mix workloads with different token distributions. This leads to noisy p95/p99 signals and slow incident triage. We also lack lightweight synthetic profiles to exercise common request shapes and a simple baseline/regression pipeline to detect changes in tokens/sec and tail latency across route/model/region slices.
proposed_solution: 1) Define 4 canonical synthetic profiles (short_turn_chat ~ 32 tokens, long_completion ~ 512 tokens, streaming_chat segmented tokens/sec, embedding_batch size 128). 2) Enhance the load harness to tag synthetic runs with profile metadata and emit per-request metrics including request_profile, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant, region, route, backend_latency_ms, service_queue_ms. 3) In the metrics pipeline, compute streaming p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec rollups per (route, model, region, request_profile) and store as separate metric series. 4) Build a Console dashboard with percentile heatmaps and time-series overlays of baseline vs current for quick comparison. 5) Implement a regression detector (rolling baseline 28d, seasonal smoothing) that opens an alert if p95 increases by >10% and absolute delta > 30ms or tokens/sec drops by >15% for >=3 consecutive evaluation windows.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic harness can run the 4 canonical profiles against hosted and Dedicated endpoints and tag every request with request_profile
Metric series for p50/p95/p99 and tokens_per_sec exist for each combination of route, model, region, and request_profile for the last 90 days
Console dashboard displays heatmap matrix of profiles vs models with selectable region and route filters
Regression detector produces reproducible alerts in staging and links to a diagnostic page with recent request samples, top kernels invoked, and KV cache hit rates
On-call playbook updated with triage steps and links to dashboards and relevant GitHub PRs
tasks: Design canonical synthetic profiles and sampling weights (Sasha)
Extend load harness to add request_profile tag and emit per-request metrics (Marco)
Add metric aggregations in pipeline: percentiles and tokens/sec rollups by labels (Infra/Observability)
Create Console dashboard with heatmaps, percentile overlay, and quick filters (Console UX)
Implement regression detector with baseline and alert rules; add suppression for known maintenance windows (SRE)
Smoke test on staging and run 48-hour continuous synthetic run to validate stability and metric cardinality (QA)
rollout_plan: Deploy metric schema changes behind a feature flag. Start with staging region for short_turn_chat profile only, validate cardinality and storage cost. Expand to remaining profiles and dedicated pools after two successful 24-hour runs. Enable alerting in a muted channel first, then escalate to on-call after one week of stable signals.
metrics_and_observability: We will emit per-request labels: request_profile, route, model_name, model_variant, region, tokens_in, tokens_out, backend_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit. Aggregations: p50/p95/p99 histogram buckets, tokens_per_sec as rate(tokens_out) per second. Store aggregated series with rollup tags for last 90 days. Dashboards will show 7d/28d baselines and delta bands.
risks_and_mitigations: Cardinality blowup from profile x model x route x region: mitigate by limiting profiles to canonical four and sampling synthetic runs at controlled cadence
Metric ingestion cost: gate rollups to aggregated series and use rollup retention policies
False positives during deploys: integrate deploy window suppression and link alerts to rollout metadata
